newsitem.title: USA: Railroads nearing deal to split Conrail - report.
newsitem.headline: Railroads nearing deal to split Conrail - report.

text.p: Executives of Conrail Inc., Norfolk Southern Corp. and CSX Corp. are nearing a deal to split Conrail lines between the two other freight railroads, the Washington Post reported on Sunday.

But sources in government, the financial community and the railroad industry, told the paper the negotiations were at a sensitive stage and could still fall apart. It was uncertain whether Conrail's board of directors would approve the deal.

A final agreement, which could be announced this week, would end Conrail's monopoly on Eastern routes, bringing multiple-railroad competition to major sections of the Northeast for the first time in 29 years.
Industry observers said the deal was likely to be approved by the National Surface Transportation Board.
The plan would divided Conrail roughly by half while giving all railroads equal access to major terminal areas such as the New York port and industrial area, the sources said.

Under the plan, CSX would get most of the main line of the former New York Central, a high-speed track up the Hudson River to Albany and Buffalo, as well as direct access to New England with Central line to Boston.
Norfolk Southern would get Conrail's "southern tier", a slower route from New York City to Buffalo, the newspaper said.
Norfolk Southern would get the main line of the former Pennsylvania Railroad from eastern Pennsylvania to Pittsburgh and west, as well as most of the former Reading Railroad.
CSX would get a line north from Philadelphia to the New York area, it added.

The newspaper gave no financial details on the deal, but quoted one congressional source as saying Conrail stockholders would still get $115 a share, double the price of the stock on the day the proposed merger of Conrail and CSX was announced.

The chairman of all three railroads met on Jan. 31 in their first effort to bridge the gap created after Norfolk Southern presented its $115-per-share hostile tender offer for Conrail stock to block CSX's cash-and-stock offer.
The companies remained mum on subsequent meetings.
